102: ### 3. Обработка триплетов
103: 
104: Из-за разнородности текста и параллельного извлечения могут появляться дублирующиеся сущности и отношения.
105: Для получения однородного узла/отношения может быть использована суммаризация, проходящая следующим образом:
106: 
107: 1. Все описания, относящиеся к одной сущности/связи, агрегируются.
108: 2. Для получения единого консистентного описания агрегированные тексты прогоняются через LLM. Этот шаг опциональный.
109: 
110: Пример:
111: 
112: * Вход:
113:  *Пётр Первый* → "русский царь"
114:   * *Пётр Великий* → "реформатор"
115: * Агрегация и суммаризация
116:   * *Пётр I (Пётр Великий)* → "Император России, проводивший масштабные реформы"
117: 
118: За этот процесс отвечают классы:
119: 
120: **`EntitySummarizer`** — агрегирование и суммаризация описаний узлов,
121: **`RelationSummarizer`** — агрегирование и суммаризация связей.
122: 
123: > В планах — добавление выравнивания (слияния) сущностей по онтологии. Для этого используется двухэтапная стратегия, позволяющая объединять разные наименования одной сущности (например: *«Пётр Первый»*, *«Император Пётр I»*, *«Пётр Великий»*).
124: >
125: > Статья: [Chepurova A. et al., 2024](https://aclanthology.org/2024.textgraphs-1.5.pdf).
126:

128: 
129: ### 4. Построение графа и выделение комьюнити
130: После выделения сущностей и отношений и их обработки происходит объединение всей информации в граф.
131: Граф хранится как направленный мультиграф: отношение сохраняет исходную сущность, целевую сущность и собственный идентификатор. Для выделения комьюнити внутри пайплайна строится ненаправленная проекция графа.
132: 
133: Для возможности ответа на абстрактивные вопросы, следуя методологии GraphRAG, применяется выделение комьюнити в графе и получение саммари по этим комьюнити.
134: Для выделения комьюнити используется [алгоритм Лейдена](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leiden_algorithm).
135: этого используется двухэтапная стратегия:
136: Затем, для каждого комьюнити генерируется саммари - текстовый отчет, описывающий ключевую смысловую составляющую, объединяющую узлы в комьюнити.
137: Отчет имеет следующий вид:
138: ```json
139: {
140:     "title": "<название_отчёта>",
141:     "summary": "<краткое_описание>",
142:     "rating": "<оценка_важности>",
143:     "rating_explanation": "<обоснование_оценки>",
144:     "findings": [
145:         {
146:             "summary": "<краткое описание вывода 1>",
147:             "explanation": "<развёрнутое объяснение вывода 1>"
148:         },
149:         {
150:             "summary": "<краткое описание вывода 2>",
151:             "explanation": "<развёрнутое объяснение вывода 2>"
152:         }
153:     ]
154: }
155: ```
156: 
157: За генерацию комьюнити саммари отвечает инструкция `community_report`.
158: 
159: На этапе получения релевантной информации для ответа на запрос пользователя этот отчет переводится в текстовый вид. Набор таких отчетов идёт как часть контекста для LLM.
160:

162: 
163: ## RAG
164: 
165: ### Локальный поиск
166: Этап локального поиска больше подходит для задачи "поиска иголки в стоге сена" - получения релевантной информации для ответа на экстрактивные вопросы, требующие небольшого ограниченного контекста.
167: Например, вопрос вида "когда умер Александр Второй?".
168: 
169: Этап локального поиска делится на:
170: 1. Поиск наиболее релевантных сущностей для запроса.
171: 2. Получение всех релевантных отношений и соседних сущностей.
172: 3. Поиск релевантных комьюнити саммари.
173: 4. Поиск чанков, из которых вся релевантная информация была выделена.
174: 
175: Релевантность сущностей определяется близостью эмбеддинга запроса к эмбеддингу описания сущности.
176: 
177: 
178: После получения всего контекста из графа, формируется его единое представление в текстовом виде. Выглядит оно следующим образом:
179: ```markdown
180: **Сущности**
181: Сущность, тип сущности, описание сущности
182: ...
183: 
184: **Отношения**
185: Сущность-источник, целевая сущность, описание отношения, ранг отношения
186: ...
187: 
188: **Саммари**
189: ...
190: 
191: **Тексты**
192: ...
193: ```
194: 
195: После получения релевантной информации, контекст и запрос подаются в LLM и итоговый ответ возвращается пользователю.
196: За получение ответа на запрос отвечает инструкция `local_search`
197: 
198: ---
199: 
200: ### Глобальный поиск
201: Глобальный поиск делится на три этапа:
202: 1. Получение релевантных комьюнити для ответа.
203: 2. Получение мета ответов на запрос по каждому полученному комьюнити. На этом этапе каждому ответу соответствует некоторая оценка релевантности (от 0 до 10).
204: 3. Все мета ответы (оценка релевантности > 0) сортируются по релевантности, а затем подаются как мета контекст вместе с запросов в LLM.
205: 
206: Мета ответы выглядят следующим образом:
207: ```json
208: {
209:     "reasoning": "<твои рассуждения о релевантности контекста>",
210:     "response": "<твой ответ>",
211:     "rating": "<оценка релевантности контекста для ответа на запрос>"
212: }
213: ```
214: 
215: За получение мета ответов отвечает инструкция `global_search_context`,
216: за получение итогового ответа — `global_search`.
217: 
218: Стоит отметить, что глобальный поиск - довольно дорогая операция :)
219:

222: ## Компоненты RAGU
223: 
224: ### Чанкеры
225: Первый шаг для построения графа знаний - разбить входной корпус сырых текстов на чанки. 
226: RAGU реализует различные подходы к разбиению, а так же поддерживает добавление своих реализаций чанкинга.
227: 
228: За интерфейс чанкера отвечает класс BaseChunker (ragu/chunker/base_chunker)
229: 
230: В RAGU доступны `SimpleChunker`, `SemanticTextChunker` и `SmartSemanticChunker`.
231: Семантический чанкер на базе `smart_chunker` представлен реализацией `SmartSemanticChunker`.
232: 
233: Детали можете найти здесь: 
234: https://github.com/anonymous-author/smart_chunker/tree/main
235: 
236: ---
237: 
238: ### Пайплайн извлечения графа
239: В RAGU реализуется три варианта извлечения графа знаний из сырых текстов: одношаговый LLM-пайплайн `ArtifactsExtractorLLM`, двухшаговый LLM-пайплайн `TwoStageArtifactsExtractorLLM` и подход на основании небольшой специализированной модели [RAGU-lm](https://huggingface.co/AnonymousTeam/RAGU-lm).
240: #### ArtifactsExtractorLLM
241: 
242: `ArtifactsExtractorLLM` - реализация классического варианта извлечения сущностей и отношений из GraphRAG, использующая LLM.
243: 
244: 
245: Пример использования:
246: ```python
247: from ragu.models.llm import LLMOpenAI
248: from ragu.models.openai import CachedAsyncOpenAI
249: from ragu.triplet import ArtifactsExtractorLLM, TwoStageArtifactsExtractorLLM
250: 
251: client = CachedAsyncOpenAI(
252:     base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1",
253:     api_key="dummy-api-token",
254:     rate_max_simultaneous=10,
255:     rate_max_per_minute=100,
256: )
257: llm = LLMOpenAI(
258:     client=client,
259:     model_name="gpt-4o-mini",
260: )
261: 
262: single_step_extractor = ArtifactsExtractorLLM(
263:     llm=llm,
264:     do_validation=True,
265: )
266: 
267: two_stage_extractor = TwoStageArtifactsExtractorLLM(
268:     llm=llm,
269:     do_entity_validation=True,
270:     do_relation_validation=True,
271: )
272: ```
273: 
274: За одношаговое выделение/валидацию элементов графа отвечают инструкции `artifact_extraction` и `artifact_validation`. Двухшаговый пайплайн использует `entity_extraction`, `entity_validation`, `relation_extraction` и `relation_validation`.
275: 
276: #### RAGU-lm
277: 
278: Для этого пайплайна используется дообученная под задачи выделения структурированной информации - [RAGU-lm](https://huggingface.co/AnonymousTeam/RAGU-lm)
279: 
280: Задачи, на которые обучена модель:
281: 1. Распознавание ненормализованных именованных сущностей из текста.
282: 2. Нормализация каждой из ненормализованных сущностей относительно текста.
283: 3. Генерация определения каждой из нормализованных именованных сущностей относительно текста.
284: 4. Генерации определения направленного отношения между парой нормализованных именованных сущностей относительно текста.
285: 
286: **System prompt**:
287: ```
288: Вы - эксперт в области анализа текстов и извлечения семантической информации из них.
289: ```
290: 
291: **Entity extraction**:
292: ```
293: Распознайте все именованные сущности в тексте и выпишите их список с новой строки.\n\nТекст: {input_text}\n\nИменованные сущности:
294: ```

441: from ragu.chunker.types import Chunk

466: ### Граф знаний
467: Для эффективного поиска релевантной информации производится индексация всех элементов графа знаний и их сохранение.
468: 
469: За хранение и доступ к элементам графа знаний отвечает класс KnowledgeGraph.
470: 
471: ```python
472: from ragu import BuilderArguments, KnowledgeGraph, SimpleChunker
473: from ragu.models.embedder import EmbedderOpenAI
474: from ragu.models.llm import LLMOpenAI
475: from ragu.models.openai import CachedAsyncOpenAI
476: from ragu.triplet import TwoStageArtifactsExtractorLLM
477: 
478: # Shared client — подходит для небольших и средних корпусов
479: client = CachedAsyncOpenAI(
480:     base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1",
481:     api_key="dummy-api-token",
482:     rate_max_simultaneous=10,
483:     rate_max_per_minute=100,
484: )
485: 
486: # Для больших корпусов (тысячи сущностей) рекомендуется использовать
487: # раздельные клиенты для LLM и эмбеддера:
488: #
489: # llm_client = CachedAsyncOpenAI(
490: #     base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1",
491: #     api_key="dummy-api-token",
492: #     rate_max_simultaneous=5,
493: #     rate_max_per_minute=60,
494: # )
495: # embed_client = CachedAsyncOpenAI(
496: #     base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1",
497: #     api_key="dummy-api-token",
498: #     rate_max_simultaneous=20,
499: #     rate_max_per_minute=500,
500: #     embed_timeout=60.0,
501: # )
502: 
503: llm = LLMOpenAI(client=client, model_name="gpt-4o-mini")
504: embedder = EmbedderOpenAI(
505:     client=client,
506:     model_name="text-embedding-3-large",
507:     dim=3072,
508: )
509: 
510: chunker = SimpleChunker(max_chunk_size=1000)
511: artifact_extractor = TwoStageArtifactsExtractorLLM(llm=llm)
512: builder_settings = BuilderArguments(
513:     use_llm_summarization=True,
514:     use_clustering=True,
515:     cluster_only_if_more_than=2,
516:     make_community_summary=True,
517: )
518: 
519: knowledge_graph = KnowledgeGraph(
520:     llm=llm,
521:     embedder=embedder,
522:     chunker=chunker,
523:     artifact_extractor=artifact_extractor,
524:     builder_settings=builder_settings,
525:     language="russian",
526: )
527: 
528: await knowledge_graph.build_from_docs(["Текстовый документ для индексации."])
529: ```
530: 
531: Сущности, отношения, саммари комьюнити и исходные чанки сохраняются через настроенные адаптеры хранилищ. Плотные векторы строятся через `embedder`; при наличии `sparse_embedder` RAGU также сохраняет разреженные векторы для гибридного поиска.

534: 
535: 
536: ### Поиск по графу знаний
537: 
538: 
539: #### Local search
540: Локальный поиск - это что-то вроде гранулированного векторного RAG. Сначала ищем top-k релевантных сущностей из графа. Затем для каждоый сущности:
541: 1. Берем все соседние сущности 
542: 2. Берем все отношения, в которых они участвуют, 
543: 3. Берем комьюнити, в который сущность состоит
544: 4. Берем чанки, из которых эти сущности были выделены.
545: 
546: Все это подается как структурированный контекст для ответа на запрос пользователя.
547: 
548: Пример использования:
549: ```python
550: from ragu.search_engine import LocalSearchEngine
551: 
552: local_search = LocalSearchEngine(
553:     llm=llm,                         # LLM для финального ответа
554:     knowledge_graph=knowledge_graph, # Граф знаний
555:     embedder=embedder,               # Эмбеддер для векторизации запроса
556: ) 
557: 
558: # Поиск релевантного контекста в графе
559: search_result = await local_search.a_search("Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши'?")
560: 
561: # Получение ответа по графу знаний 
562: response = await local_search.a_query("Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши'?")
563: print(response.response)
564: ```
565: 
566: 
567: #### Global Search
568: Глобальный поиск - поиск по комьюнити в графе.
569: 
570: Алгоритм:
571: 1. Берем каждое комьюнити из графа.
572: 2. Получаем ответ на запрос по каждому комьюнити саммари.
573: Каждый ответ содержит так же оценку его полезности для итогового ответа на запрос (от 0 до 10).
574: 3. Получаем итоговый ответ на запрос, взяв в качестве контекста ответы с предыдущего этапа, отсортированные по релевантности.
575: 
576: ```python
577: from ragu.search_engine import GlobalSearchEngine
578: 
579: global_search = GlobalSearchEngine(
580:     llm=llm,
581:     knowledge_graph=knowledge_graph,
582: )
583: 
584: # Поиск релевантного контекста в графе
585: search_result = await global_search.a_search("Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши'?")
586: 
587: # Получение ответа по графу знаний 
588: response = await global_search.a_query("Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши'?")
589: print(response.response)
590: ```
591: 
592: #### Naive Search
593: 
594: Naive search - это векторный RAG по исходным чанкам. Он не расширяет контекст через соседей в графе, а ищет релевантные чанки в векторном хранилище и передает их в LLM.
595: 
596: ```python
597: from ragu.search_engine import NaiveSearchEngine
598: 
599: naive_search = NaiveSearchEngine(
600:     llm=llm,
601:     knowledge_graph=knowledge_graph,
602:     embedder=embedder,
603: )
604: 
605: # Поиск релевантных чанков
606: search_result = await naive_search.a_search("Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши'?")
607: 
608: # Получение ответа по найденным чанкам
609: response = await naive_search.a_query("Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши'?")
610: print(response.response)
611: ```
612: 
613: #### Mix Search
614: 
615: Mix search запускает несколько поисковых движков и просит LLM собрать итоговый ответ из их результатов. Это полезно, когда нужен одновременно локальный графовый контекст, векторный контекст по чанкам и контекст по комьюнити.
616: 
617: ```python
618: from ragu.search_engine import MixSearchEngine
619: 
620: mix_search = MixSearchEngine(
621:     llm=llm,
622:     engines=[local_search, naive_search, global_search],
623: )
624: 
625: response = await mix_search.a_query("Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши'?")
626: print(response.response)
627: ```
628: 
629: #### Query Planning
630: 
631: `QueryPlanEngine` оборачивает любой поисковый движок и разбивает сложный вопрос на зависимые подзапросы перед формированием итогового ответа.
632: 
633: ```python
634: from ragu.search_engine import QueryPlanEngine
635: 
636: planned_search = QueryPlanEngine(local_search)
637: 
638: response = await planned_search.a_query(
639:     "Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши' и из какой страны был автор?"
640: )
641: print(response.response)
642: ```
643: 
644: Пример декомпозиции запроса:
645: 
646: ```python
647: subqueries = await planned_search.process_query(
648:     "Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши' и из какой страны был автор?"
649: )
650: 
651: for subquery in subqueries:
652:     print(subquery.id, subquery.query, subquery.depends_on)
653: 
654: # Возможный результат:
655: # q1 Кто написал роман 'Камо Грядеши'? []
656: # q2 Из какой страны был автор? ['q1']
657: ```

661: ### Prompt tuning
662: 
663: У каждого класса, который использует LLM под капотом, можно поменять используемую инструкцию.
664: 
665: Сейчас все инструкции представлены классом `RAGUInstruction`.
666: ```python
667: @dataclass
668: class RAGUInstruction:
669:     messages: ChatMessages
670:     pydantic_model: Type[BaseModel] | Type[str] = str
671:     description: str | None = None
672: ```
673: 
674: Получение словаря вида `"название_инструкции" : "соответствующий_prompt_template"`:
675: ```python
676: from ragu import LocalSearchEngine
677: 
678: search_engine = LocalSearchEngine(
679:     llm=llm,
680:     knowledge_graph=knowledge_graph,
681:     embedder=embedder,
682: )
683: 
684: print(search_engine.get_prompts())
685: 
686: local_search_prompt = search_engine.get_prompt("local_search")
687: print(local_search_prompt.messages.to_str())
688: ```
689: 
690: Обновление инструкции:
691: ```python
692: from textwrap import dedent
693: 
694: from ragu.common.prompts.messages import ChatMessages, SystemMessage, UserMessage
695: from ragu.common.prompts.prompt_storage import RAGUInstruction
696: 
697: search_engine.update_prompt(
698:     "local_search",
699:     RAGUInstruction(
700:         messages=ChatMessages.from_messages([
701:             SystemMessage(content="Отвечай только на основе переданного контекста графа."),
702:             UserMessage(content=dedent(
703:                 """
704:                 Запрос: {{ query }}
705:                 Контекст: {{ context }}
706:                 Язык: {{ language }}
707:                 """
708:             )),
709:         ]),
710:         pydantic_model=str,
711:         description="Пользовательская инструкция для local search",
712:     ),
713: )
714: ```

По главному расхождению — устаревшему классу `PromptTemplate` — **русская версия изначально была корректна**: в ней (`docs/ru/ragu_components.md:665-672`) правильно используется `RAGUInstruction`, а не `PromptTemplate`. Именно поэтому я её не менял. EN-док был «отстающим» по этому пункту, и я подтянул его до уровня RU.

## Но при полном перечитывании нашёл два мелких расхождения

### 1. Сниппет `RAGUInstruction` (строки 667–672) — неполный

В RU-доке:
```python
@dataclass
class RAGUInstruction:
    messages: ChatMessages
    pydantic_model: Type[BaseModel] | Type[str] = str
    description: str | None = None
```

Реальный код (`ragu/common/prompts/prompt_storage.py:52-57`) и моя правка EN-дока:
```python
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RAGUInstruction:
    messages: ChatMessages
    pydantic_model: Type[BaseModel] | Type[str] = str
    description: str | None = None
    few_shot_formatter: FewShotFormatter | None = None
```

То есть в RU не хватает:
- декоратора `(frozen=True, slots=True)` (показан просто `@dataclass`);
- поля `few_shot_formatter`.

### 2. Текстовый «огрызок» в разделе 4 (строки ~134–136)

Там сейчас:
```
…применяется выделение комьюнити в графе и получение саммари по этим комьюнити.
Для выделения комьюнити используется алгоритм Лейдена.
этого используется двухэтапная стратегия:        ← висящий фрагмент, не связан с соседями
Затем, для каждого комьюнити генерируется саммари…
```

Фраза «этого используется двухэтапная стратегия:» — это, судя по всему, мусор/огрызок от прошлой редакции. В EN-версии этого нет — там чисто: алгоритм Лейдена → `community_report` генерирует саммари. Стоит удалить фрагмент и привести абзац в соответствие с EN.

## Чего в RU-доке НЕТ (и не нужно)

Упоминаний Memgraph и `multi_stage_artifacts_extractor.py` я не нашёл (grep и ручная проверка подтвердили). NEREL-таблицы, чанкеры, экстракторы, `KnowledgeGraph(..., language="russian")`, поисковые движки, `QueryPlanEngine` — всё сверено с кодом, расхождений нет.

## Предлагаемый план (2 мелкие правки)

1. **Строки 667–672**: дополнить сниппет `RAGUInstruction` декоратором `(frozen=True, slots=True)` и полем `few_shot_formatter` — для паритета с кодом и EN-версией.
2. **Строки ~134–136**: удалить висящий фрагмент «этого используется двухэтапная стратегия:» и связать абзац (алгоритм Лейдена → `community_report`).

Это точечные правки, не влияющие на код. Подтвердить — и я внесу их (когда выйдем из plan-режима)? Или оставить RU как есть, поскольку по сути он уже корректен?

+++ b/tests/common/test_global_parameters.py
@@ -0,0 +1,222 @@
+"""
+Tests for GlobalSettings: Literal-typed backends and save/load serialization.
+"""
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+from typing import Literal, get_args, get_origin, get_type_hints
+
+from ragu.common.global_parameters import GlobalSettings, Settings
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def isolated_settings():
+    """Snapshot and restore Settings to prevent singleton leakage."""
+    snapshot = Settings._serializable_dict()
+    working_dir_snapshot = Settings._working_dir
+    yield Settings
+    for name, value in snapshot.items():
+        setattr(Settings, name, value)
+    Settings._working_dir = working_dir_snapshot
+
+
+# --- Literal typing ---------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_tokenizer_backend_fields_are_literal():
+    hints = get_type_hints(GlobalSettings)
+    assert get_args(hints["tokenizer_embedder_backend"]) == ("tiktoken", "local")
+    assert get_args(hints["tokenizer_llm_backend"]) == ("tiktoken", "local")
+    assert get_origin(hints["tokenizer_embedder_backend"]) is Literal
+
+
+def test_default_backend_values():
+    assert Settings.tokenizer_embedder_backend == "tiktoken"
+    assert Settings.tokenizer_llm_backend == "tiktoken"
+
+
+# --- save / load round-trip -------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_save_writes_all_serializable_fields(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "settings.json"
+    Settings.save(out)
+
+    data = json.loads(out.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    assert set(data.keys()) == {
+        "language",
+        "tokenizer_embedder_backend",
+        "tokenizer_llm_backend",
+        "tokenizer_embedder_name",
+        "tokenizer_llm_name",
+        "embedder_token_limit",
+        "llm_token_limit",
+        "llm_context_token_limit",
+    }
+
+
+def test_save_excludes_storage_folder(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "settings.json"
+    Settings.save(out)
+
+    data = json.loads(out.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    assert "storage_folder" not in data
+    assert "_working_dir" not in data
+    assert "_current_time" not in data
+
+
+def test_save_captures_instance_overrides(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    Settings.embedder_token_limit = 123
+    Settings.tokenizer_embedder_backend = "local"
+    Settings.language = "russian"
+
+    out = tmp_path / "settings.json"
+    Settings.save(out)
+
+    data = json.loads(out.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    assert data["embedder_token_limit"] == 123
+    assert data["tokenizer_embedder_backend"] == "local"
+    assert data["language"] == "russian"
+
+
+def test_round_trip_restores_values(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    Settings.embedder_token_limit = 555
+    Settings.tokenizer_llm_backend = "local"
+    Settings.tokenizer_llm_name = "custom-llm"
+    Settings.llm_context_token_limit = 12_000
+
+    out = tmp_path / "settings.json"
+    Settings.save(out)
+
+    # Mutate to different values, then reload.
+    Settings.embedder_token_limit = 1
+    Settings.tokenizer_llm_backend = "tiktoken"
+    Settings.tokenizer_llm_name = "gpt-4o"
+    Settings.llm_context_token_limit = 30_000
+
+    Settings.load(out)
+
+    assert Settings.embedder_token_limit == 555
+    assert Settings.tokenizer_llm_backend == "local"
+    assert Settings.tokenizer_llm_name == "custom-llm"
+    assert Settings.llm_context_token_limit == 12_000
+
+
+def test_load_does_not_touch_storage_folder(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "settings.json"
+    Settings.save(out)
+
+    original_dir = Settings._working_dir
+    Settings.storage_folder = "/some/other/path"
+
+    Settings.load(out)
+
+    assert Settings._working_dir == "/some/other/path"
+    # restore for the fixture's own teardown bookkeeping
+    Settings._working_dir = original_dir
+
+
+# --- validation on load -----------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_load_rejects_invalid_literal_backend(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "bad.json"
+    out.write_text(
+        json.dumps({"tokenizer_embedder_backend": "fasttoken"}),
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="tokenizer_embedder_backend"):
+        Settings.load(out)
+
+
+def test_load_rejects_non_positive_int(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "bad.json"
+    out.write_text(
+        json.dumps({"embedder_token_limit": 0}),
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="positive integer"):
+        Settings.load(out)
+
+
+def test_load_rejects_wrong_int_type(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "bad.json"
+    out.write_text(
+        json.dumps({"embedder_token_limit": "8192"}),
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="expected int"):
+        Settings.load(out)
+
+
+def test_load_rejects_bool_for_int(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "bad.json"
+    out.write_text(
+        json.dumps({"embedder_token_limit": True}),
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="expected int"):
+        Settings.load(out)
+
+
+def test_load_rejects_wrong_str_type(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "bad.json"
+    out.write_text(
+        json.dumps({"language": 42}),
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="expected str"):
+        Settings.load(out)
+
+
+def test_load_rejects_non_object_json(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "bad.json"
+    out.write_text("[1, 2, 3]", encoding="utf-8")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="JSON object"):
+        Settings.load(out)
+
+
+def test_load_rejects_invalid_json(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "bad.json"
+    out.write_text("{not valid json", encoding="utf-8")
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Failed to read"):
+        Settings.load(out)
+
+
+def test_load_rejects_missing_file(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "missing.json"
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Failed to read"):
+        Settings.load(out)
+
+
+def test_load_ignores_unknown_keys(isolated_settings, tmp_path, caplog):
+    out = tmp_path / "extra.json"
+    out.write_text(
+        json.dumps({
+            "embedder_token_limit": 256,
+            "mystery_field": "ignored",
+        }),
+        encoding="utf-8",
+    )
+    Settings.load(out)
+    assert Settings.embedder_token_limit == 256
+
+
+# --- save filesystem behavior -----------------------------------------------
+
+
+def test_save_creates_parent_directories(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out = tmp_path / "nested" / "deep" / "settings.json"
+    Settings.save(out)
+    assert out.exists()
+
+
+def test_save_pathlib_and_str_equivalent(isolated_settings, tmp_path):
+    out_str = tmp_path / "as_str.json"
+    Settings.save(str(out_str))
+    assert out_str.exists()
+
+    out_path = tmp_path / "as_path.json"
+    Settings.save(out_path)
+    assert out_path.exists()

+---
+
+#### Token Limits and Settings
+
+RAGU centralises token-limit and tokenizer configuration in the `Settings` singleton. These defaults are used by `EmbedderOpenAI` (for embedding input truncation) and search engines (for LLM context truncation).
+
+```python
+from ragu import Settings
+
+# Embedder truncation (applied automatically inside EmbedderOpenAI)
+Settings.embedder_token_limit = 8_192                    # max tokens per embedding input
+Settings.tokenizer_embedder_backend = "tiktoken"         # "tiktoken" or "local"
+Settings.tokenizer_embedder_name = "text-embedding-3-large"
+
+# LLM context truncation (applied by search engines before answer generation)
+Settings.llm_token_limit = 32_798                        # max tokens for LLM inputs during indexing
+Settings.llm_context_token_limit = 30_000                # max tokens for search-engine context
+Settings.tokenizer_llm_backend = "tiktoken"              # "tiktoken" or "local"
+Settings.tokenizer_llm_name = "gpt-4o"
+
+# Example: using a local BGE model with 512-token context
+# pip install graph_ragu[local]
+Settings.embedder_token_limit = 512
+Settings.tokenizer_embedder_backend = "local"
+Settings.tokenizer_embedder_name = "BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5"
+```
+
+Per-instance overrides on `EmbedderOpenAI` take precedence over `Settings`:
+
+```python
+embedder = EmbedderOpenAI(
+    client=embed_client,
+    model_name="BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5",
+    embedder_token_limit=512,
+    tokenizer_backend="local",
+    tokenizer_name="BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5",
+)
+```
+
+---
+
+#### Serializing Global Settings
+
+When running benchmarks or reproducible experiments, it is useful to store the
+RAGU configuration alongside the produced artifacts. `GlobalSettings` exposes
+two explicit methods for this — `save(path)` writes a JSON snapshot and
+`load(path)` restores it. Serialization is **never** invoked automatically
+(there are no constructor/destructor hooks): you decide when to persist and
+reload.
+
+```python
+from ragu import Settings
+
+# Persist the current configuration next to your experiment artifacts.
+Settings.save("./runs/exp_42/ragu_settings.json")
+
+# Later, in a fresh process, reproduce the exact same configuration.
+Settings.load("./runs/exp_42/ragu_settings.json")
+```
+
+What gets serialized: `language`, `tokenizer_embedder_backend`,
+`tokenizer_llm_backend`, `tokenizer_embedder_name`, `tokenizer_llm_name`,
+`embedder_token_limit`, `llm_token_limit`, `llm_context_token_limit`.
+
+What does **not** get serialized:
+
+- `storage_folder` — by default it contains a runtime timestamp, and restoring
+  it silently would redirect subsequent writes into a stale directory. Manage
+  the storage folder explicitly if you need to reproduce it.
+- Internal state (singleton handle, the current timestamp).
+
+`load` validates every value against the declared type hints and raises
+`ValueError` on a mismatch (e.g. an unknown tokenizer backend or a non-positive
+token limit). Unknown keys in the file are reported via a warning and ignored,
+so files produced by a newer RAGU version remain loadable.

+## local_embedder_with_short_context.py
+
+End-to-end example that uses a **local embedding model with a short context window** (e.g., BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 with 512 tokens) served via vLLM, alongside a remote LLM API.
+
+### What it does
+
+1. Configures `Settings` with the embedder's token limit (512) and a HuggingFace tokenizer
+2. Creates separate `CachedAsyncOpenAI` clients for the LLM (remote) and the embedder (local vLLM)
+3. Builds a knowledge graph with automatic text truncation before embedding
+4. Runs local search queries
+
+### Prerequisites
+
+- RAGU installed with local tokenizer support (`pip install -e ".[local]"`)
+- A local vLLM server serving an embedding model:
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve intfloat/multilingual-e5-large --port 8001   # Multilingual, 512 tokens
+  # or
+  vllm serve BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 --port 8001           # English only, 512 tokens
+  ```
+- An OpenAI-compatible LLM API endpoint
+- Environment variables:
+  - `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LLM_MODEL_NAME` — LLM configuration
+  - `LOCAL_EMBEDDER_URL` — local embedder endpoint (e.g., `http://localhost:8001/v1`)
+  - `EMBEDDER_MODEL_NAME` — embedding model name (e.g., `intfloat/multilingual-e5-large` or `BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5`)
+
+### Key configuration points
+
+- **Choosing an embedder**: Use a multilingual model (e.g. `intfloat/multilingual-e5-large`) for non-English corpora. English-only models (e.g. `BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5`) produce lower-quality vectors on Russian text, which degrades retrieval precision and can lead to incorrect answers.
+- **Token limit**: Set via `Settings.embedder_token_limit` to match the model's context window (512 for both models above). `Settings.tokenizer_embedder_backend = "local"` enables the HuggingFace tokenizer. The LLM tokenizer backend (`Settings.tokenizer_llm_backend`) remains `"tiktoken"` by default and is independent.
+- **Retrieval precision**: A smaller or less capable embedder may require a larger `top_k` in `a_query()` (e.g. `top_k=40` instead of the default 20) to compensate for lower vector similarity quality.

+"""
+Example: building and querying a knowledge graph with a local embedding model
+that has a short context window (e.g. 512 tokens).
+
+This demonstrates the ``Settings`` configuration for tokenizer and token limits,
+as well as separate ``CachedAsyncOpenAI`` clients for the LLM and the local
+embedder served via `vLLM <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm>`_.
+
+Choosing an embedder for your language
+~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
+- **English only**: ``BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5`` (512 tokens).
+- **Multilingual / Russian**: ``intfloat/multilingual-e5-large`` (512 tokens).
+
+Adjust ``Settings.embedder_token_limit`` to match the model's context window.
+A smaller or less capable embedder may require a larger ``top_k`` in
+``a_query()`` to compensate for lower retrieval precision.
+
+Usage
+-----
+1. Start the local embedder with vLLM.
+   Use ``--enforce-eager`` to avoid CUDA assertion errors with some
+   models (e.g. ``intfloat/multilingual-e5-large``)::
+
+        vllm serve intfloat/multilingual-e5-large --port 8001 --enforce-eager
+
+2. Export environment variables::
+
+       export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://..."       # LLM API endpoint
+       export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
+       export LLM_MODEL_NAME="gpt-4o-mini"
+       export LOCAL_EMBEDDER_URL="http://localhost:8001/v1"
+       export EMBEDDER_MODEL_NAME="intfloat/multilingual-e5-large"
+
+3. Run::
+
+       python examples/local_embedder_with_short_context.py
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import os
+
+from ragu import (
+    ArtifactsExtractorLLM,
+    BuilderArguments,
+    KnowledgeGraph,
+    LocalSearchEngine,
+    Settings,
+    SimpleChunker,
+)
+from ragu.common.prompts import ICLConfig
+from ragu.models.embedder import EmbedderOpenAI
+from ragu.models.llm import LLMOpenAI
+from ragu.models.openai import CachedAsyncOpenAI
+from ragu.utils.ragu_utils import read_text_from_files
+
+
+async def main():
+    # ── Global settings ─────────────────────────────────────────────
+    Settings.storage_folder = "ragu_working_dir/local_embedder_example"
+    Settings.language = "russian"
+
+    # Configure token limits and tokenizer for the local embedder.
+    # These defaults are used by EmbedderOpenAI unless overridden per-instance.
+    #
+    # IMPORTANT: choose an embedder that matches your language:
+    #   English  → BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5   (512 tokens)
+    #   Multilingual / Russian → intfloat/multilingual-e5-large (512 tokens)
+    #
+    # Set embedder_token_limit to match the model's context window.
+    Settings.embedder_token_limit = 512
+    Settings.tokenizer_embedder_backend = "local"
+    Settings.tokenizer_embedder_name = os.getenv("EMBEDDER_MODEL_NAME")
+
+    # ── Load documents ──────────────────────────────────────────────
+    docs = read_text_from_files("examples/data/ru")
+
+    chunker = SimpleChunker(max_chunk_size=1000)
+
+    # ── LLM client (remote API) ────────────────────────────────────
+    llm_client = CachedAsyncOpenAI(
+        base_url=os.getenv("OPENAI_BASE_URL"),
+        api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY"),
+        rate_max_simultaneous=10,
+        rate_max_per_minute=100,
+    )
+
+    llm = LLMOpenAI(
+        client=llm_client,
+        model_name=os.getenv("LLM_MODEL_NAME"),
+    )
+
+    # ── Embedder client (local vLLM) ───────────────────────────────
+    embed_client = CachedAsyncOpenAI(
+        base_url=os.getenv("LOCAL_EMBEDDER_URL"),
+        api_key="unused",
+        rate_max_simultaneous=20,
+        rate_max_per_minute=500,
+        embed_timeout=60.0,
+    )
+
+    # batch_size=32 and max_concurrent_batches=2 are tuned for a local GPU.
+    # Defaults (500 and 5) are designed for cloud APIs and may cause OOM on vLLM.
+    embedder = EmbedderOpenAI(
+        client=embed_client,
+        model_name=os.getenv("EMBEDDER_MODEL_NAME"),
+        embedder_token_limit=512,
+        tokenizer_backend="local",
+        tokenizer_name=os.getenv("EMBEDDER_MODEL_NAME"),
+        batch_size=32,
+        max_concurrent_batches=2,
+    )
+    await embedder.initialize()
+
+    # ── Build knowledge graph ───────────────────────────────────────
+    icl_config = ICLConfig(
+        enabled=True,
+        num_examples=2,
+        selection_strategy="hybrid",
+    )
+
+    artifact_extractor = ArtifactsExtractorLLM(
+        llm=llm,
+        embedder=embedder,
+        icl_config=icl_config,
+        do_validation=True,
+    )
+
+    builder_settings = BuilderArguments(
+        use_llm_summarization=True,
+        vectorize_chunks=True,
+    )
+
+    knowledge_graph = KnowledgeGraph(
+        llm=llm,
+        embedder=embedder,
+        chunker=chunker,
+        artifact_extractor=artifact_extractor,
+        builder_settings=builder_settings,
+    )
+    await knowledge_graph.build_from_docs(docs)
+
+    # ── Query ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+    search_engine = LocalSearchEngine(
+        llm=llm,
+        knowledge_graph=knowledge_graph,
+        embedder=embedder,
+    )
+
+    questions = [
+        "Кто написал гимн Норвегии?",
+        "Шум, издаваемый ЭТИМИ ПАУКООБРАЗНЫМИ, слышен за пять километров. Отсюда и их название.",
+        "Как переводится название романа 'Ка́мо гряде́ши, Го́споди?' на русский языке"
+    ]
+
+    for question in questions:
+        print(f"\nQ: {question}")
+        # top_k=40 compensates for lower retrieval precision of smaller embedders
+        answer = await search_engine.a_query(question, top_k=40)
+        print(f"A: {answer}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    asyncio.run(main())

## Summary

- **Centralized tokenizer & token-limit configuration** in the `Settings` singleton:
  new typed fields `tokenizer_embedder_backend`, `tokenizer_llm_backend`,
  `tokenizer_embedder_name`, `tokenizer_llm_name`, `embedder_token_limit`,
  `llm_token_limit`, `llm_context_token_limit` (with `Literal["tiktoken","local"]` validation).
- **`EmbedderOpenAI` now auto-truncates** input to `Settings.embedder_token_limit` tokens
  before every API call (per-instance overrides via constructor). The `context_truncator`
  plumbing was removed from `Index` / `KnowledgeGraph` — truncation now lives inside the embedder.
- **Search engines** no longer accept `max_context_length` / `tokenizer_backend` /
  `tokenizer_model`; `BaseEngine` reads these from `Settings`.
- **`TokenTruncation` (local backend)** now accounts for special tokens (`[CLS]`/`[SEP]`),
  fixing silent over-limit requests against BGE/E5-style models.
- **`Settings.save(path)` / `Settings.load(path)`** — JSON serialization of the config
  (Literal/int/str validation; `storage_folder` deliberately excluded) for reproducible runs.
- **Bugfix:** SQLite `database disk image is malformed` corruption resolved via `sqlite_synchronous=2`.
- New example `examples/local_embedder_with_short_context.py` (local vLLM embedder, 512-token context);
  README, AGENTS.md and subpackage READMEs updated.

## Compatibility

Configuration 255: 256: #### Builder Settings 257: 258: Configure the knowledge graph building pipeline using `BuilderArguments`: 259: 260: ```python 261: from ragu import BuilderArguments 262: 263: builder_arguments = BuilderArguments( 264: use_llm_summarization=True, # Enable LLM-based entity/relation summarization 265: use_clustering=False, # Apply clustering before summarization. Use it if your text contains many similar entities. 266: build_only_vector_context=False, # Skip graph extraction, only chunk embeddings 267: make_community_summary=True, # Generate community summaries 268: remove_isolated_nodes=True, # Remove entities without relations 269: vectorize_chunks=True, # Vectorize chunk for naive (vector) search 270: cluster_only_if_more_than=10000, # Minimum entities before clustering kicks in 271: summarize_only_if_more_than=7, # Summarize descriptions only when there are many duplicates 272: max_cluster_size=128, # Maximum entities per cluster 273: random_seed=42, 274: ) 275: 276: # Pass to KnowledgeGraph 277: knowledge_graph = KnowledgeGraph( 278: llm=llm, 279: embedder=embedder, 280: chunker=chunker, 281: artifact_extractor=artifact_extractor, 282: builder_settings=builder_arguments, 283: ) 284: await knowledge_graph.build_from_docs(docs) 285: ``` 286: 287: Common builder presets: 288: 289: ```python 290: # Naive vector RAG only: chunks + chunk vectors, no entity/relation graph. 291: BuilderArguments( 292: build_only_vector_context=True, 293: make_community_summary=False, 294: ) 295: 296: # Fast graph extraction: no extra LLM summarization and no communities. 297: BuilderArguments( 298: use_llm_summarization=False, 299: use_clustering=False, 300: make_community_summary=False, 301: remove_isolated_nodes=True, 302: ) 303: 304: # Full GraphRAG: extraction, summarization, communities, global search support. 305: BuilderArguments( 306: use_llm_summarization=True, 307: use_clustering=False, 308: make_community_summary=True, 309: remove_isolated_nodes=True, 310: ) 311: ``` 312: 313: --- 314: 315: #### Client and Rate Limiting Configuration 316: 317: `CachedAsyncOpenAI` is the network-level client shared by `LLMOpenAI` and `EmbedderOpenAI`. It controls rate limiting, retries, caching, and timeouts. 318: 319: **Shared client (simpler, works for most cases):** 320: 321: ```python 322: client = CachedAsyncOpenAI( 323: base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1", 324: api_key="sk-...", 325: rate_max_simultaneous=10, 326: rate_max_per_minute=100, 327: cache="./llm_cache", 328: ) 329: 330: llm = LLMOpenAI(client=client, model_name="gpt-4o-mini") 331: embedder = EmbedderOpenAI(client=client, model_name="text-embedding-3-large", dim=3072) 332: ``` 333: 334: **Separate clients (recommended for large corpora or different providers):** 335: 336: When processing large corpora (thousands of entities and relations), LLM calls (slow, seconds per request) and embedding calls (fast but numerous) compete for the same connection pool and rate limiter. Using separate clients isolates their resources: 337: 338: ```python 339: llm_client = CachedAsyncOpenAI( 340: base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1", 341: api_key="sk-...", 342: rate_max_simultaneous=5, 343: rate_max_per_minute=60, 344: retry_times_sec=(4, 8, 16), 345: cache="./llm_cache", 346: ) 347: 348: embed_client = CachedAsyncOpenAI( 349: base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1", # can be a different provider 350: api_key="sk-...", 351: rate_max_simultaneous=20, 352: rate_max_per_minute=500, 353: embed_timeout=60.0, 354: cache="./embed_cache", 355: ) 356: 357: llm = LLMOpenAI(client=llm_client, model_name="gpt-4o-mini") 358: embedder = EmbedderOpenAI( 359: client=embed_client, 360: model_name="text-embedding-3-large", 361: dim=3072, 362: batch_size=500, 363: max_concurrent_batches=5, 364: ) 365: ``` 366: 367: **When a shared client is sufficient:** 368: - Small to medium documents (up to ~1000 entities/relations) 369: - Generous API provider rate limits 370: - Both LLM and embedder use the same endpoint 371: 372: **When separate clients are recommended:** 373: - Large corpora (thousands of entities and relations) 374: - Strict API rate limits (low RPM) 375: - LLM and embedder on different providers or endpoints 376: - You need independent scaling of LLM vs. embedding throughput 377: 378: **Key parameters:** 379: 380: | Parameter | Description | Default | 381: |-----------|-------------|---------| 382: | `rate_max_simultaneous` | Max concurrent in-flight requests | None (unlimited) | 383: | `rate_max_per_minute` | Max requests per minute | None (unlimited) | 384: | `rate_min_delay` | Min seconds between request starts | None | 385: | `retry_times_sec` | Retry wait schedule on transient errors | `(2, 4, 8)` | 386: | `embed_timeout` | Per-request timeout for embedding calls (seconds) | `60.0` | 387: | `cache` | Cache directory path | None | 388: 389: `EmbedderOpenAI` also accepts: 390: 391: | Parameter | Description | Default | 392: |-----------|-------------|---------| 393: | `batch_size` | Max texts per single API call | `500` | 394: | `max_concurrent_batches` | Max concurrent batch API calls | `5` | 395: | `embedder_token_limit` | Max tokens per input text (overrides `Settings`) | `None` | 396: | `tokenizer_backend` | Tokenizer: `"tiktoken"` or `"local"` (overrides `Settings`) | `None` | 397: | `tokenizer_name` | Tokenizer model ID (overrides `Settings`) | `None` | 398: 399: All input texts are automatically truncated to the token limit before being sent to the embedding API. The limit defaults to `Settings.embedder_token_limit` (8192) and can be overridden per `EmbedderOpenAI` instance. 400: 401: --- 402: 403: #### Token Limits and Settings 404: 405: RAGU centralises token-limit and tokenizer configuration in the `Settings` singleton. These defaults are used by `EmbedderOpenAI` (for embedding input truncation) and search engines (for LLM context truncation). 406: 407: ```python 408: from ragu import Settings 409: 410: # Embedder truncation (applied automatically inside EmbedderOpenAI) 411: Settings.embedder_token_limit = 8_192 # max tokens per embedding input 412: Settings.tokenizer_embedder_backend = "tiktoken" # "tiktoken" or "local" 413: Settings.tokenizer_embedder_name = "text-embedding-3-large" 414: 415: # LLM context truncation (applied by search engines before answer generation) 416: Settings.llm_token_limit = 32_798 # max tokens for LLM inputs during indexing 417: Settings.llm_context_token_limit = 30_000 # max tokens for search-engine context 418: Settings.tokenizer_llm_backend = "tiktoken" # "tiktoken" or "local" 419: Settings.tokenizer_llm_name = "gpt-4o" 420: 421: # Example: using a local BGE model with 512-token context 422: # pip install graph_ragu[local] 423: Settings.embedder_token_limit = 512 424: Settings.tokenizer_embedder_backend = "local" 425: Settings.tokenizer_embedder_name = "BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5" 426: ``` 427: 428: Per-instance overrides on `EmbedderOpenAI` take precedence over `Settings`: 429: 430: ```python 431: embedder = EmbedderOpenAI( 432: client=embed_client, 433: model_name="BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5", 434: embedder_token_limit=512, 435: tokenizer_backend="local", 436: tokenizer_name="BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5", 437: ) 438: ``` 439: 440: --- 441: 442: #### In-Context Learning (Few-Shot Examples) 443: 444: RAGU extractors can use few-shot examples to improve extraction quality. When enabled, the extractor selects relevant examples and includes them in the LLM prompt. Four selection strategies are available: 445: 446: | Strategy | Description | Requires `embedder` | 447: |----------|-------------|:---:| 448: | `"semantic"` | Cosine similarity on dense embeddings (default) | Yes | 449: | `"bm25"` | Lexical matching via BM25 — fast, no API calls | No | 450: | `"hybrid"` | Reciprocal Rank Fusion of semantic + BM25 rankings | Yes | 451: | `"random"` | Uniform random sampling — useful as a baseline | No | 452: 453: ```python 454: from ragu.common.prompts import ICLConfig 455: 456: icl_config = ICLConfig( 457: enabled=True, # Enable/disable ICL 458: num_examples=2, # Number of examples per extraction call (1-3 recommended) 459: selection_strategy="semantic", # "semantic" | "bm25" | "hybrid" | "random" 460: ) 461: 462: artifact_extractor = TwoStageArtifactsExtractorLLM( 463: llm=llm, 464: embedder=embedder, # Required for "semantic" and "hybrid"; optional for "bm25" and "random" 465: icl_config=icl_config, 466: ) 467: ``` 468: 469: Both `ArtifactsExtractorLLM` and `TwoStageArtifactsExtractorLLM` support ICL. An `embedder` is required for `"semantic"` and `"hybrid"` strategies; for `"bm25"` and `"random"` it can be omitted. Pre-built example files ship with RAGU in `ragu/common/prompts/icl_examples/`. 470: 471: To generate custom examples for your domain, use the generation script: 472: 473: ```bash 474: python scripts/generate_icl_examples.py --config config/icl_generation.yaml 475: ``` 476: 477: --- 478: 479: 480: ### Knowledge Graph Construction 481: Each text in corpus is processed to extract structured information. 1: # Module: ragu.common
2: 
3: ## Role in RAGU Pipeline
4: 
5: `ragu.common` provides cross-cutting infrastructure for the whole GraphRAG pipeline: global settings, prompt rendering, logging, batching, and cache helpers. It is not a pipeline stage by itself, but every stage depends on it.
6: 
7: Pipeline position:
8: 
9: ```text
10: settings + prompts + utilities
11:   -> chunking / extraction / graph building / storage / retrieval / generation
12: ```
13: 
14: ## Overview
15: 
16: The module keeps shared behavior out of the domain packages. It centralizes the default storage directory, default filenames, runtime environment loading, prompt templates, and the base class used by LLM-driven modules.
17: 
18: ## Key Components
19: 
20: ### Settings
21: 
22: Singleton instance of `GlobalSettings`.
23: 
24: - Purpose: stores process-wide defaults.
25: - Important fields: `language`, `storage_folder`.
26: - Used by: storage initialization, prompts, builders, search engines, sparse embedders.
27: 
28: ```python
29: from ragu.common.global_parameters import Settings
30: 
31: Settings.language = "english"
32: Settings.storage_folder = "./ragu_working_dir/demo"
33: Settings.init_storage_folder()
34: 
35: print(Settings.storage_folder)
36: ```
37: 
38: ### Env
39: 
40: Pydantic settings model.
41: 
42: - Purpose: load model API configuration from environment variables or `.env`.
43: - Important fields: `llm_model_name`, `llm_base_url`, `llm_api_key`, optional embedder and reranker fields.
44: 
45: ```python
46: from ragu.common.env import Env
47: 
48: env = Env(
49:     llm_model_name="gpt-4o-mini",
50:     llm_base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1",
51:     llm_api_key="dummy-api-token",
52: )
53: 
54: print(env.llm_model_name)
55: ```
56: 
57: ### RaguGenerativeModule
58: 
59: Base class for modules that own prompts.
60: 
61: - Purpose: load default prompts by name or accept custom `RAGUInstruction` objects.
62: - Important methods: `get_prompt`, `get_prompts`, `update_prompt`.
63: - Used by: extractors, summarizers, and search engines.
64: 
65: ```python
66: from ragu.common.base import RaguGenerativeModule

85: ### ChatMessages and Message Types
86: 
87: Prompt-message abstraction from `ragu.common.prompts.messages`.
88: 
89: - Purpose: represent system/user/assistant messages and convert them to OpenAI chat payloads.
90: - Important classes: `SystemMessage`, `UserMessage`, `AIMessage`, `ChatMessages`.
91: 
92: ```python
93: from ragu.common.prompts.messages import ChatMessages, SystemMessage, UserMessage
94: 
95: messages = ChatMessages.from_messages([
96:     SystemMessage(content="Answer briefly."),
97:     UserMessage(content="What is RAGU?"),
98: ])
99: 
100: print(messages.to_openai())
101: ```
102: 
103: ### render
104: 
105: Jinja2 renderer for prompt messages.
106: 
107: - Purpose: render one or many conversations from scalar and batch parameters.
108: - Important behavior: list/tuple parameters define batch size; all batch parameters must have the same length.
109: 
110: ```python
111: from ragu.common.prompts.messages import ChatMessages, UserMessage, render
112: 
113: template = ChatMessages.from_messages([
114:     UserMessage(content="Question: {{ query }}")
115: ])
116: 
117: rendered = render(template, query=["What is RAGU?", "What is GraphRAG?"])
118: print([conversation.to_str() for conversation in rendered])
119: ```
120: 
121: ### BatchGenerator
122: 
123: Small batching helper used by rerankers and utility code.
124: 
125: ```python
126: from ragu.common.batch_generator import BatchGenerator
127: 
128: generator = BatchGenerator([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], batch_size=2)
129: print(list(generator.get_batches()))
130: ```
131: 
132: ### get_cache
133: 
134: Disk cache helper that returns a mutable mapping backed by `diskcache`.
135: 
136: ```python
137: from ragu.common.cache import get_cache
138: 
139: cache = get_cache("./ragu_working_dir/cache")
140: cache["key"] = {"value": 1}
141: print(cache["key"])
142: ```
143: 
144: ## Data Flow
145: 
146: Input: runtime configuration, prompt names, prompt parameters.
147: 
148: Output: storage paths, rendered `ChatMessages`, OpenAI-compatible message lists, cache mappings.
149: 
150: Used by:
151: 
152: - `ragu.triplet` extraction prompts
153: - `ragu.graph` summarization prompts and storage defaults
154: - `ragu.search_engine` answer-generation prompts
155: - `ragu.models` caching and API wrappers
156: 
157: ## Usage Examples
158: 
159: ### Example 1 - Minimal usage
160: 
161: ```python
162: from ragu.common.global_parameters import Settings
163: 
164: Settings.language = "english"
165: Settings.storage_folder = "./ragu_working_dir/example"
166: Settings.init_storage_folder()
167: 
168: print(Settings.storage_folder)
169: ```
170: 
171: ### Example 2 - Pipeline usage
172: 
173: ```python
174: from ragu.common.prompts.messages import ChatMessages, SystemMessage, UserMessage, render
175: 
176: template = ChatMessages.from_messages([
177:     SystemMessage(content="Answer in {{ language }}."),
178:     UserMessage(content="Question: {{ query }}\nContext: {{ context }}"),
179: ])
180: 
181: rendered = render(
182:     template,
183:     language="english",
184:     query=["What is RAGU?", "What is local search?"],
185:     context=["GraphRAG system", "Entity-neighborhood retrieval"],
186: )
187: 
188: openai_messages = [conversation.to_openai() for conversation in rendered]
189: print(openai_messages[0])
190: ```
191: 
192: ### Example 3 - Change an instruction in a generative module
193: 
194: ```python
195: from ragu.common.base import RaguGenerativeModule
196: from ragu.common.prompts.messages import ChatMessages, UserMessage, render
197: from ragu.common.prompts.prompt_storage import RAGUInstruction
198: 
199: module = RaguGenerativeModule(prompts=["local_search"])
200: module.update_prompt(
201:     "local_search",
202:     RAGUInstruction(
203:         messages=ChatMessages.from_messages([
204:             UserMessage(
205:                 content=(
206:                     "Use only the context below. "
207:                     "Answer in {{ language }}.\n\n"
208:                     "Context:\n{{ context }}\n\n"
209:                     "Question: {{ query }}"
210:                 )
211:             )
212:         ]),
213:         pydantic_model=str,
214:         description="Strict context-only local search prompt.",
215:     ),
216: )
217: 
218: instruction = module.get_prompt("local_search")
219: rendered = render(
220:     instruction.messages,
221:     language="english",
222:     context="Python is a programming language.",
223:     query="What is Python?",
224: )[0]
225: 
226: print(rendered.to_openai())
227: ```
228: 
229: ## Integration Points
230: 
231: - LLMs: `ChatMessages.to_openai()` produces payloads accepted by `LLM.chat_completion`.
232: - Extraction and retrieval: `RaguGenerativeModule` loads named prompts from `DEFAULT_PROMPT_TEMPLATES`.
233: - Storage: `Settings.storage_folder` and `DEFAULT_FILENAMES` define default locations for KV, vector, and graph files.
234: - Configuration: `Env.from_env()` loads OpenAI-compatible model settings for application entrypoints.
235: 
236: ## Configuration
237: 
238: Environment variables consumed by `Env`:
239: 
240: - `llm_model_name`, `llm_base_url`, `llm_api_key`
241: - `embedder_base_url`, `embedder_api_key`, `embedder_model_name`
242: - `reranker_base_url`, `reranker_api_key`, `reranker_model_name`
243: 
244: Global defaults:
245: 
246: - `Settings.language = "english"`
247: - `Settings.storage_folder` defaults to `./ragu_working_dir/<timestamp>`.
248: 
249: ## Dependencies
250: 
251: Internal:
252: 
253: - `ragu.common.prompts`
254: - `ragu.common.logger`
255: 
256: External:
257: 
258: - `pydantic-settings`
259: - `jinja2`
260: - `diskcache`
261: - `loguru`
262: - OpenAI SDK message types
263: 
264: ## Notes / Pitfalls
265: 
266: - `Settings` is global process state. Set `Settings.storage_folder` before constructing `KnowledgeGraph` or `Index`.
267: - Jinja rendering uses `StrictUndefined`; missing template variables raise errors.
268: - `render()` treats any list or tuple parameter as batched input.
269: - Default prompt names must exist in `DEFAULT_PROMPT_TEMPLATES`, otherwise `get_prompt()` can return `None` at construction time and fail later.

50: \author{
51:   Anonymous \\
52:   \textit{Under review at EMNLP 2026 Industry Track}
53: }
54: 
55: \date{}
56: 
57: \begin{document}
58: 
59: \maketitle
60: 
61: \begin{abstract}
62: Graph retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) enhances large language
63: models with structured knowledge, yet existing systems such as LightRAG
64: construct knowledge graphs in a single extraction pass, producing noisy
65: entities and brittle retrieval.
66: We start from a simple observation: the capabilities required of an LLM
67: inside a RAG pipeline---comprehension, extraction, and reasoning over
68: context---are language skills that, unlike factual world knowledge, grow
69: only weakly with model size.
70: This insight yields two contributions.
71: First, a compact 7\,B model optimized for language skills rather than
72: factual recall, which outperforms Qwen2.5-32B on knowledge-graph
73: construction (a +12.5\% relative gain in harmonic mean on our
74: information-extraction benchmark) and matches a same-size general model
75: on English GraphRAG tasks.
76: Second, a modular GraphRAG engine that separates extraction from
77: consolidation: entities and relations pass through two-stage extraction,
78: DBSCAN-backed deduplication, LLM summarization, and hierarchical Leiden
79: community detection before indexing.
80: On GraphRAG-Bench (Medical), our engine improves answer correctness by up
81: to 4$\times$ over LightRAG across four difficulty levels while raising
82: evidence recall from 0.71 to 0.84.
83: A size ablation shows that extraction LLMs from 3\,B to 14\,B yield nearly
84: identical downstream quality, confirming the language-knowledge hypothesis.
85: Model, engine, and the new information-extraction benchmark are released
86: under Apache\,2.0 (links anonymized for review).
87: \end{abstract}
88: 
89: % ===================================================================
90: \section{Introduction}
91: \label{sec:intro}
92: 
93: Retrieval-augmented generation~(RAG) has become the standard paradigm for
94: grounding large language models (LLMs) in external knowledge~\cite{lewis2020rag,gao2023rag_survey}.
95: Traditional RAG systems split documents into flat chunks, embed them in a
96: vector space, and retrieve the top-$k$ at query time---an approach that cannot
97: capture the relational structure connecting entities across documents.
98: Graph RAG~(GraphRAG) addresses this by building a knowledge graph from the
99: corpus and using graph traversal during
100: retrieval~\cite{edge2024graphrag,guo2025lightrag,gutierrez2025hipporag2}.
101: Despite conceptual advances, practical adoption faces three obstacles.
102: 
103: \paragraph{Obstacle 1: Single-pass extraction.}
104: Current GraphRAG systems treat knowledge graph construction as a single LLM
105: extraction pass, producing noisy, duplicated entities with no mechanism to
106: \emph{consolidate} information across chunks.
107: 
108: \paragraph{Obstacle 2: Dependence on expensive LLMs.}
109: Because extraction quality directly determines graph quality, practitioners
110: default to large API models (GPT-4-class), making GraphRAG expensive.
111: This dependence rests on a false premise: the capabilities an LLM needs
112: \emph{inside} a RAG pipeline---comprehension, extraction, reasoning over
113: provided context---are \emph{language skills}, not factual recall.
114: As Section~\ref{sec:hypothesis} shows, language skills grow only weakly
115: with model size, while world knowledge scales steeply.
116: A compact, skill-oriented model is therefore sufficient.
117: 
118: \paragraph{Obstacle 3: Engineering immaturity.}
119: Several open-source frameworks suffer from installation failures or
120: inconsistent APIs.\footnote{During benchmarking, we encountered frameworks
121:   that could not be installed without manual patching.
122:   LightRAG~\cite{guo2025lightrag} is a notable exception.}
123: A GraphRAG engine should be both \emph{semantically} strong and
124: \emph{engineerable}: installable, maintainable, and deployable on
125: cost-effective hardware.
126: 
127: We address all three obstacles with two artifacts:
128: \menolite{}, a 7\,B model fine-tuned from
129: RuadaptQwen2.5-7B-Lite-Beta~\cite{tihomirov2025ruadapt_model} for
130: RAG-oriented language skills, and \ragu{}, a modular GraphRAG engine whose
131: pipeline separates extraction from consolidation---chunking, entity/relation
132: extraction, DBSCAN-backed summarization, Leiden community detection, and
133: community summarization.
134: 
135: Our contributions are:
136: \begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
137:   \item We articulate and empirically validate the \emph{language/world
138:         knowledge hypothesis}: world knowledge scales markedly with model
139:         size, whereas language skills---all that a RAG-internal LLM
140:         requires---do not, justifying compact extractor models
141:         (Section~\ref{sec:hypothesis}).
142:   \item \menolite{}, a 7\,B domain-adapted LLM optimized for language skills
143:         (information extraction, multi-hop reasoning, summarization) that
144:         rivals models up to $\sim$4$\times$ larger on knowledge graph
145:         construction.
146:   \item \ragu{}, an engineering-mature, modular multi-step GraphRAG engine
147:         that separates extraction from consolidation, yielding cleaner and
148:         more connected knowledge graphs.
149:   \item Extensive evaluation under fixed conditions across four GraphRAG
150:         benchmarks (GraphRAG-Bench, BioASQ, MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA)
151:         and three Russian language benchmarks (MERA, LIBRA, and our own
152:         information-extraction benchmark based on the NEREL schema).
153:         Both artifacts will be released under Apache\,2.0.\footnote{Anonymized
154:         code and model links are provided in supplementary materials.}
155: \end{enumerate}
156: 
157: % ===================================================================
158: \section{The Language/World Knowledge Hypothesis}
159: \label{sec:hypothesis}
160: 
161: We hypothesize that \textbf{world knowledge}---facts, entities, and their
162: relationships---scales (near-)linearly with parameter count, whereas
163: \textbf{language skills}---comprehension, extraction, inference over provided
164: context---scale markedly more slowly with parameter count.
165: If so, a RAG pipeline (where external knowledge comes from the retrieval
166: subsystem) should function well with a compact, skill-oriented model.
167: 
168: \paragraph{Motivating experiment.}
169: We evaluate the Qwen2.5-Instruct family~\cite{yang2024qwen2} (0.5\,B--72\,B) on
170: two MERA~\cite{fenogenova2024mera} tasks:
171: \emph{CheGeKa}~\cite{taktasheva-etal-2022-tape} (quiz-style QA requiring world
172: knowledge) and \emph{MultiQ} (multi-hop QA where all facts are in-context).
173: 
174: % Figure 1: World knowledge vs language skills scaling
175: \begin{figure}[t]
176: \centering
177: \includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/llm_quality.png}
178: \caption{Effect of model size on world-knowledge (CheGeKa) vs.\
179:   language-skill (MultiQ) tasks in the Qwen2.5-Instruct family.
180:   CheGeKa F1 increases 21.1$\times$ from 0.5\,B to 72\,B; MultiQ F1 increases
181:   only 4$\times$---despite a 144$\times$ increase in parameters.
182:   Results are F1 scores on the MERA benchmark~\cite{fenogenova2024mera}.}
183: \label{tab:hypothesis}
184: \end{figure}
185: 
186: As Figure~\ref{tab:hypothesis} shows, CheGeKa F1 increases 21.1$\times$ from 0.5\,B
187: to 72\,B, while MultiQ F1 increases only 4$\times$ despite a 144$\times$
188: parameter increase.\footnote{Log-linear regression slopes are in
189: Appendix~\ref{app:scaling}.}
190: In a GraphRAG pipeline, the LLM extracts entities, summarizes descriptions,
191: and generates answers from context---all language skills, not world-knowledge
192: tasks. \menolite{} (Section~\ref{sec:meno}) is designed as an empirical test
193: of this prediction.
194: 
195: % ===================================================================
196: \section{Related Work}
197: \label{sec:related}
198: 
199: \paragraph{Graph RAG.}
200: Microsoft GraphRAG~\cite{edge2024graphrag} builds knowledge graphs via LLM
201: extraction and Leiden communities; LightRAG~\cite{guo2025lightrag} adds
202: dual-level retrieval and incremental updates;
203: HippoRAG\,2~\cite{gutierrez2025hipporag2} uses personalized PageRank;
204: Wikontic~\cite{chepurova2026wikontic} enforces ontological constraints.
205: GraphRAG-Bench~\cite{xiang2026graphragbench} provides a systematic comparison.
206: \ragu{} differs by introducing an explicit \emph{multi-step consolidation}
207: stage and by targeting engineering maturity.
208: 
209: \paragraph{Compact and domain-adapted LLMs.}
210: General-purpose chat models~\cite{yang2024qwen2,brown2020language} are
211: expensive for extraction; Russian-adapted models such as
212: RuadaptQwen2.5~\cite{tihomirov2025ruadapt_model} improve language quality but
213: are not optimized for IE. \menolite{} is trained specifically for RAG-oriented
214: language skills over the NEREL schema~\cite{loukachevitch2021nerel},
215: operationalizing the hypothesis from Section~\ref{sec:hypothesis}.
216: 
217: % ===================================================================
218: \section{System Design}
219: \label{sec:ragu}
220: 
221: \subsection{Multi-Step Graph Construction}
222: \label{sec:pipeline}
223: 
224: Our pipeline processes documents through six configurable stages
225: (engineering details in Appendix~\ref{app:engineering}; the end-to-end
226: data flow is visualized in Appendix~\ref{app:dataflow}):
227: 
228: \paragraph{Step 1: Chunking.}
229: Three strategies: \emph{SimpleChunker} (fixed-size overlapping chunks),
230: \emph{SemanticTextChunker} (embedding-based split points), and
231: \emph{SmartSemanticChunker} (cross-encoder reranking).
232: 
233: \paragraph{Step 2: Entity \& Relation Extraction.}
234: \emph{(a)}~Single-stage: one prompt extracts entities and relations per chunk.
235: \emph{(b)}~Two-stage (Figure~\ref{fig:architecture}): entities are extracted
236: and validated first, then relations are extracted constrained to the
237: identified entity set, which prevents spurious entity--relation mismatches
238: and sharpens extraction precision; the standalone extraction quality of
239: \menolite{} is reported in Table~\ref{tab:nerel}.\footnote{The exact prompts are listed in
240: Appendix~\ref{app:prompts}, and a worked extraction example appears in
241: Appendix~\ref{app:trace_extraction}.}
242: All strategies use the NEREL schema~\cite{loukachevitch2021nerel} (29 entity
243: types, 49 relation types) with optional ICL (semantic, BM25, hybrid, random).
244: 
245: \begin{figure*}[t]
246:   \centering
247:   \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/architecture_two_stage.png}
248:   \caption{Architecture of the two-stage extractor.
249:     Stage~1 extracts entities from each chunk and validates them against the
250:     NEREL schema; Stage~2 extracts relations constrained to the validated
251:     entity set, eliminating spurious entity--relation mismatches.
252:     Optional in-context-learning (ICL) examples are injected at both stages.
253:     A concrete extraction trace is shown in Appendix~\ref{app:trace_extraction}.}
254:   \label{fig:architecture}
255: \end{figure*}
256: 
257: \paragraph{Step 3: Entity \& Relation Summarization.}
258: \emph{The key consolidation stage absent from prior GraphRAG systems.}
259: \emph{EntitySummarizer} groups entities by (name, type) and---for entities
260: with many duplicate mentions---applies DBSCAN clustering and LLM summarization.
261: \emph{RelationSummarizer} follows the same pattern.
262: Reducing noise \emph{before} community detection produces a cleaner graph
263: (Appendix~\ref{app:trace_consolidation} illustrates this consolidation
264: stage on a worked example).
265: 
266: \paragraph{Step 4--6: Community Detection, Summarization, Refinement.}
267: Hierarchical Leiden clustering partitions the deduplicated graph; an LLM
268: generates structured community reports (title, summary, findings); pluggable
269: modules (e.g., \texttt{RemoveIsolatedNodes}) optionally refine the graph.
270: 
271: \subsection{Search Engines}
272: \label{sec:search}
273: 
274: \ragu{} provides five engines: \textbf{LocalSearch} (vector-similarity entity
275: retrieval expanded to relations and chunks), \textbf{GlobalSearch} (LLM-rated
276: community summarization), \textbf{NaiveSearch} (standard vector RAG),
277: \textbf{MixSearch} (parallel multi-engine), and \textbf{QueryPlanEngine} (DAG
278: decomposition). All support cross-encoder reranking and hybrid dense+sparse
279: retrieval via Qdrant.
280: 
281: \subsection{Engineering and Deployment}
282: \label{sec:engineering}
283: 
284: \ragu{} is designed as a production-ready Python package
285: (Table~\ref{tab:eng_comparison} in Appendix~\ref{app:engineering_details}
286: provides a detailed comparison).
287: \emph{(i)}~A three-tier storage abstraction
288: (\texttt{BaseStorage}~$\to$~graph/KV/vector) with lifecycle callbacks
289: enables backend swapping (NetworkX$\to$Neo4j, NanoVDB$\to$Qdrant).
290: \emph{(ii)}~An async-first API with bounded concurrency provides
291: production-safe throughput; synchronous wrappers are auto-generated.
292: \emph{(iii)}~A strictly typed, memory-efficient domain model prevents integration errors at development time; structured LLM outputs are validated through Pydantic v2, removing manual JSON post-processing.
293: \emph{(iv)}~Incremental upsert/update/delete with deterministic hash-based
294: IDs and merge policies, plus a consistency auditor verifying cross-store
295: integrity.
296: The system supports single-GPU deployment with a 7\,B extraction model.
297: 
298: % ===================================================================
299: \section{Compact Model}
300: \label{sec:meno}
301: 
302: \subsection{Design Philosophy}
303: 
304: Our design inverts the usual LLM training paradigm: rather than storing
305: knowledge in parameters, we externalize it into a retrieval corpus and train
306: the model to \emph{process} context effectively---investing compute in
307: language skills, not world knowledge.
308: 
309: \subsection{Training Pipeline}
310: 
311: \menolite{} is derived from
312: RuadaptQwen2.5-7B-Lite-Beta~\cite{tihomirov2025ruadapt_model} through:
313: \emph{Stage~1:}~Continued Pretraining (1.3B tokens, Russian+English
314: educational/scientific texts, quality-filtered with
315: gte-multilingual-base~\cite{li2023generaltextembeddingsmultistage}); \emph{Stage~2:}~Supervised
316: Fine-Tuning (50M tokens) covering NEREL-based
317: extraction~\cite{loukachevitch2021nerel}, multi-hop QA from
318: MultiHop-RAG~\cite{tang2024multihop} and MTRAGEval~\cite{Katsis2025mtrag},
319: and LightRAG~\cite{guo2025lightrag} query logs. The critical distinction:
320: instructions teach the model to \emph{use context} rather than \emph{recall
321: facts}.
322: 
323: \subsection{Key Properties}
324: 
325: \menolite{} achieves the highest harmonic mean (0.468) on our IE benchmark,
326: outperforming Qwen2.5-32B (0.416) and gemma-3-27B (0.396). It has a 128K
327: context window (passkey retrieval 0.98 at 128K), 47\% better tokenizer
328: efficiency than vanilla Qwen2.5 on Russian text (3.77 vs.\ 2.57
329: chars/token; per-model measurements are documented in the supplementary
330: model card, anonymized for review),
331: and fits on a single consumer GPU via vLLM~\cite{kwon2023efficient}.
332: 
333: % ===================================================================
334: \section{Experiments}
335: \label{sec:experiments}
336: 
337: \subsection{Experimental Setup}
338: \label{sec:setup}
339: 
340: We test three hypotheses:
341: \textbf{H1}---language skills scale more slowly with model size than world
342: knowledge (\S\ref{sec:hypothesis}; Figure~\ref{tab:hypothesis});
343: \textbf{H2}---a multi-step consolidation pipeline yields richer context than
344: single-pass extraction; \textbf{H3}---a compact 7\,B model is a drop-in
345: replacement for larger models inside a GraphRAG pipeline.
346: 
347: \paragraph{Group~1: GraphRAG Pipeline Evaluation.}
348: We compare \ragu{} against LightRAG~\cite{guo2025lightrag},
349: HippoRAG\,2~\cite{gutierrez2025hipporag2}, and NaiveRAG on four
350: benchmarks:
351: \emph{GraphRAG-Bench}~\cite{xiang2026graphragbench} (Medical domain;
352: four difficulty levels: fact retrieval, complex reasoning, contextual
353: summarize, creative generation),
354: \emph{BioASQ}~\cite{BioASQ2023} (biomedical QA),
355: \emph{MuSiQue}~\cite{trivedi2022musique} (multi-hop QA), and
356: \emph{2WikiMultiHopQA}~\cite{ho2020multihopqa} (multi-hop reasoning).
357: 
358: \textbf{Fixed conditions.} All systems use the \emph{same} answer-generation
359: LLM (gpt-4o-mini), isolating the effect of graph construction.
360: On GraphRAG-Bench, we use BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 for embeddings; on the
361: other three benchmarks, gte-multilingual-base~\cite{li2023generaltextembeddingsmultistage}.
362: Graph construction LLMs are varied as independent variables.
363: 
364: \textbf{Metrics.} Generation quality is measured by \emph{Answer
365: Correctness} (AC; LLM-judge) and \emph{ROUGE-L} (RL) on all benchmarks.
366: GraphRAG-Bench additionally reports \emph{Coverage} (Cov) and
367: \emph{Faithfulness} (Faith) for Levels~3--4.
368: Retrieval quality (GraphRAG-Bench only) uses \emph{Evidence Recall} (ER)
369: and \emph{Context Relevancy} (CR).
370: All LLM-as-judge evaluations use \texttt{google/gemini-3-flash-preview}
371: with \texttt{openai/text-embedding-3-small} for embedding-based
372: sub-metrics, ensuring no evaluator--generator overlap.
373: 
374: \paragraph{Group~2: Model Evaluation.}
375: We evaluate \menolite{} on
376: \emph{MERA}~\cite{fenogenova2024mera} (overall score and tasks relevant
377: to RAG: MultiQ, RWSD, RCB, CheGeKa, ruWorldTree),
378: \emph{LIBRA}~\cite{libra2025} (long-context passkey retrieval at
379: 4\,K--128\,K tokens; LibrusecMHQA multi-hop QA), and
380: our own \emph{IE benchmark} based on the NEREL
381: dataset~\cite{loukachevitch2021nerel} (knowledge-graph
382: construction: NER, relation extraction, entity/relation definitions;
383: fully documented in Appendix~\ref{app:ie_benchmark}).
384: Baselines: Qwen2.5-7B/14B/32B-Instruct, T-lite-it-1.0/2.1,
385: AvitoTech/avibe, RuadaptQwen2.5-7B-Lite-Beta, gemma-3.
386:

420: \subsection{GraphRAG-Bench Results}
421: \label{sec:graphragbench}
422: 
423: Table~\ref{tab:gen_medical} reveals a dramatic gap: \ragu{} improves
424: Answer Correctness by 2--4$\times$ over LightRAG, with the advantage growing
425: with task complexity (2.1$\times$ on Fact Retrieval vs.\ 4.1$\times$ on
426: Creative Generation). LightRAG's higher ROUGE-L is a length artifact:
427: LightRAG answers average 25 words vs.\ 130 for \ragu{}, and ROUGE-L
428: penalizes the longer, more informative responses. Answer Correctness,
429: which is length-normalized, confirms \ragu's superiority.
430:

454: 
455: Retrieval results (Table~\ref{tab:retrieval_medical}) confirm that
456: \ragu's advantage originates at context formation: Evidence Recall rises
457: from 71--76\% (LightRAG) to 76--84\%, directly supporting Hypothesis~2.
458: Crucially, the within-RAGU ablation
459: (Tables~\ref{tab:ablation_gen}--\ref{tab:ablation_ret}) shows that the ICL
460: and validation toggles each shift Answer Correctness by at most
461: $\sim$1.5\,pp, so the 2--4$\times$ gap over single-pass LightRAG cannot be
462: attributed to those options; it reflects the aggregate effect of \ragu's
463: structural choices---two-stage typed extraction, entity/relation
464: summarization, and community-based local retrieval---over single-pass
465: free-form extraction.
466: 
467: \paragraph{Model size does not affect graph quality.}
468: Replacing the 3\,B Qwen2.5-3B with the 7\,B Qwen2.5-7B changes Answer
469: Correctness by at most 1\,pp, validating Hypothesis~3. A detailed ablation
470: (ICL, validation) is in Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}.

518: graph-traversal retrieval (HippoRAG\,2) for multi-hop chain reasoning, and
519: consolidation-based retrieval (\ragu{}) for context-completeness tasks.

521: extraction model, while HippoRAG\,2 relies on GPT-4-class API calls.

598: \label{sec:cost}

600: A key practical advantage is cost: with a locally served extraction model
601: (\menolite{} on a single GPU), graph construction replaces per-token API
602: charges with a fixed GPU cost. Among the baselines, only MS-GraphRAG depends
603: on a commercial GPT-4-class API ($\sim$40\,k indexing tokens/doc at
604: gpt-4o rates~\cite{openai_pricing}); the open baselines (LightRAG,
605: HippoRAG\,2) use a local model under the same GPU regime, and answer
606: generation uses gpt-4o-mini for all systems. See Appendix~\ref{app:cost}.
